 Follow Iowa Volunteers Pack 990,864 Meals for World-Record Hunger Relief
 AGDAILY Wed, October 21, 2026 at 10:30 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Volunteers packed 990,864 meals in Des Moines, Iowa. (Image by World Food Prize Foundation) More than 1,000 volunteers in Des Moines, Iowa, packaged 990,864 hunger relief meals in a single hour on Tuesday, claiming the Guinness World Records title for packaging the greatest number of hunger relief meals within a one-hour span, according to the World Food Prize Foundation. The total nearly doubled the previous record of 530,064.
 The World Food Prize Foundation and Meals from the Heartland led the attempt, which closed opening day of the 2026 Borlaug Dialogue as the World Food Prize observed its 40th anniversary.
 Across 60 tables, each staffed by 16 volunteers, crews filled upward of 43 boxes per table within the hour. A single box holds four large bags that together make 216 individual meals. Each meal blends rice, soy protein, dehydrated vegetables, vitamins and minerals into six servings that cook with boiling water.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The record was verified on site by Thomas Bradford, an official Guinness World Records adjudicator.
 Iowa communities will receive half the meals, while the rest go to communities worldwide. In all, organizers estimate the meals will feed roughly 2,037 children for a full year.
 "Iowa has always known how to roll up its sleeves and get the job done, and tonight our volunteers did exactly that," said Thomas Vilsack, CEO of the World Food Prize Foundation and a former U.S. Ag Secretary. "Packaging almost a million meals in one hour is a world record, but more importantly, it's thousands of people who will have nutritious food for a year."
 The Borlaug Dialogue continues through Thursday at the Iowa Events Center.
